title: Print `gh auth refresh` for 401 returns
body:
`gh auth refresh` exists to make it simpler for users to refresh their tokens on expiration/scope mismatch, but help messages only suggest using it in limited scenarios, and not in a common case of a token expiring and the user receiving a 401 error. Now, the auth flow will detect this case, and for refreshable tokens (namely, tokens created by logging in with `gh auth login` in the first place), it will suggest using `gh auth refresh` for these cases.

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/13066.

`gh auth refresh` exists to make it simpler for users to refresh their tokens on expiration/scope mismatch, but help messages only suggest using it in limited scenarios, and not in a common case of a token expiring and the user receiving a 401 error. issues.title: Print `gh auth refresh` instead of `gh auth login` when the user encounters a 401
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

`gh auth refresh` exists as a useful, quick reauthentication mechanism for users, but the existing error messages around `gh` operations due to expired tokens do not suggest this; instead, they suggest `gh auth login`, which has a number of extra steps involved.

### Proposed solution

Instead of printing `gh auth login` when a token generated by `gh auth login` returns a 401, print `gh auth refresh`, so the user knows about the simpler path.

### Additional context

Don't think there's anything else to add here.
comments: Hey @333fred, I think you're looking for `gh auth refresh`. Let me know if that works! 🙌

It probably depends on the command and what headers we are getting back. We do print `gh auth refresh` messages but I think only when there are scope mismatches with the requirements of the API. Printing this sort of thing on 401s is interesting - initial thoughts are I don't know if that would cause any complications. Certainly we'd have to check the token type at least.

Thanks @333fred. I do think I'm going to close this out though unless you want to revise the issue title & body for this new request? Let me know what you'd like to do, or if you'd prefer to make a new issue. Either one is fine with me.

🙌 I read it @333fred, thank you. I think that seems very reasonable. I have a couple unexplored questions about the correct token source strings to assert on (and also some comments about how these probably should be constants somewhere but that's not a problem you've introduced here 😆 ), but that can wait for the PR.

I think we could fit that PR review in sometime if you open it. I'll flag this issue for the team to discuss and prioritize. Cheers.
